benchmark: Direct Parquet versus Table API at one, two and eight DuckDB threads
binary_note: All configurations used the same shell, built from the parallel-reader changes before their commit.

settings.summary: Median of executions 1 and 2, excluding first-use execution 0

method: Fresh native DuckDB process per mode/workload, with three queries in that process.
Direct-files and Table API two-thread data reused from the immediately preceding comparison.
One-thread and eight-thread Table API measurements were collected afterwards, not interleaved by thread count.
SQL wall time includes binding and execution; token acquisition is outside the SQL timing.
No OS or service cache flush, and no common source snapshot guarantee.
All reported aggregate results matched across modes, repetitions and thread counts.
COUNT and counted LIMIT can avoid reading the named Price column; these are not forced Price-value scans.
Stream counters instrument Table API only; they do not measure direct-file HTTP traffic.
Duration counters ending in _ns are elapsed times, not client process CPU.
Peak-active streams is a connection high-water snapshot, not an additive per-query counter.
Every successful Table API query returned one stream. The reader used its serial fast path at all thread settings.

excluded_attempts.reason: Child process failure; the runner at that point did not retain a sanitized reason or partial timings.
excluded_attempts.handling: Preserved as a failed attempt. Aggregate was rerun once separately with fresh credentials; filter and no-match cases then ran separately. The cause was not established.
